# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found three things on this bomb: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. The brackets mean I have no idea what any of them hold — I can't read the display, and wire colours mean nothing to me. I am the only one who can act, and the only action I have is cutting a wire position, so nothing gets cut until I know exactly which position is safe.

The real problem is the wiring between us, not the bomb: I can hear, but I can't see. Mute has the manual but no voice — whatever Mute learns can never reach me directly, only through Deaf, who sees gestures but hears nothing and can talk. So the pipeline has to be Mute → (gestures) → Deaf → (speech) → me. Deaf also sees everything printed on the bomb, so Deaf is my source for display contents, the light's state and colour, and each wire's colour in order. Right now I know nothing about what Mute or Deaf perceive; nothing has reached me at all.

So this turn I do two things: tell Mute the full tactile structure and spell out the relay plan, and gesture to Deaf to speak to me — 👋 for attention, 🫵 for "you", 🤙 as in "call me". No cutting, no risky moves until words come back.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking. My hands found: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. I can feel them but cannot read anything printed and cannot tell colours. I can hear you, but you cannot speak to me and Deaf cannot hear at all — so the only route to me is: you gesture the manual's instructions to Deaf, and Deaf speaks them aloud to me. Please look up the manual sections for the display, the light and the wires, and also tell Deaf (by gesture) that I need Deaf to say aloud: what the display shows, whether the light is on and its colour, and the colour of each wire in order, 1 through 3. If the manual needs anything else printed on the bomb, Deaf can see all of it. I will not cut anything until Deaf has spelled out exactly which position to cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🤙"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this is Deaf, answering your hello. I cannot hear anything you say, ever: talk to Mute, and gesture anything meant for me. The bomb as I see it: display 0, light white, three wires numbered 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Mute has the manual and is teaching me a sign code right now; from next round I will relay Mute's instructions to you out loud here. Touch and explore if you like, but cut, press, pull or release nothing until Mute's rules arrive through me and are confirmed.

Deaf's report reached me and it matches my hands exactly: three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, plus a display and a light. Now I also have the printed layer by proxy — display reads 0, light is white, wires are yellow, green, blue in that order. The relay is working: Deaf can speak to me directly, so once Mute's rules reach Deaf, they reach me.

Two things left to do before any cutting, and this turn is for setting them up. First, Mute can't see the bomb, so I should hand Mute the bomb's full state — that way Mute can look up exactly the right manual sections and tailor the instructions to display 0, a white light, and yellow/green/blue wires. Second, I need to acknowledge Deaf, who lives entirely in gestures, so Deaf knows the message landed and that I'm holding steady.

I'll speak the bomb's state and my requests to Mute, and gesture a simple confirmation to Deaf: 👍 for received, ✋ for hold/wait — I will not touch anything beyond what I've already felt, and I'll cut only on Deaf's spoken word.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: the relay works — Deaf has spoken me the bomb's full printed state. Here is everything we know so you can find the right rules: the display reads 0, the light is white, and the wires in position order are 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. My hands confirm there are exactly three wires, a display, and a light, nothing else. Please look up the manual for these cases and gesture the full instructions to Deaf: especially which wire position I must cut given these colours together with this display and light, and what role the display and light play if the wire rule depends on them. Spell out any conditions in words simple enough for Deaf to relay verbatim. Deaf will speak your rules aloud to me next round. I will cut nothing until then.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I received your thumbs-up and raised hand, and I read that as: understood, holding still. If the raised hand meant something else, gesture me again and I will ask until we match. News from my eyes: the light on the bomb has changed from white to purple, display still 0. Mute has not replied yet this round; I expect the first confirmed rules next round and will speak them to you the moment I have them. Until then: explore with your hands all you want, but cut, press, pull or release nothing.

The big news is that the light changed on its own — white to purple — while display held at 0. That changes my picture of the bomb: the light is dynamic, so any rule tied to its colour is time-sensitive. Mute is currently looking up rules for a white light, which may already be stale. I must get the update to Mute this turn, and I should push for rules in conditional form ("if the light is X, cut position Y") so that a last-second change doesn't leave me waiting another round. I'll also ask Mute to instruct Deaf to re-report the display and light right before I cut, since Mute and Deaf can coordinate in gesture directly.

To Deaf, a gesture-only acknowledgment: 👍 understood, ✋ hold, 🤙 keep speaking to me. Deaf already saw the light change — Deaf is the one who reported it — so no need to inform Deaf, only to keep the channel open and the hold in place.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, urgent update: the light is NOT white anymore. It changed by itself to purple between rounds; the display still reads 0. The light is dynamic, so please find the rule as conditionals: for each possible light colour, which wire position I cut; and what role the display value plays, including for display 0 specifically. Wire order is still 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Also, please gesture Deaf a request: immediately before I cut, Deaf must re-check the display and light and speak me their current values together with the cut instruction, so the rule is applied to fresh state. Deaf expects to relay your first rules to me next round. I am still holding — no cuts until your rules arrive through Deaf.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋", "🤙"])
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, update: the light is red this round — the sequence so far is white, then purple, then red. Display still 0, wires untouched: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. I read your ? ? ? as: understood, holding still, keep me posted — this is the post. Mute has stayed silent for two rounds, so I have just answered Mute in sign, echoing the code Mute taught me and proposing signs for cut, press, grab, release, zero, and the colours. Here is where you can help directly: you can speak, and Mute can hear. Tell Mute aloud, in your own words, that Deaf received the first lesson, answered it in sign, and is waiting for the code confirmation and the rules — your voice is the only push Mute can get besides my gestures. And if anything changes under your fingers — a button, a panel edge, the ends of the wires, the display surface — report it to me by gesture, since your words never reach me. Touch and map all you like; cut, press, pull or release nothing.

Deaf's post tells me two things: the light keeps cycling (white → purple → red, one step per round), and Mute has gone quiet for two rounds — the relay's middle link is stalled. Deaf is right that my voice is the only lever on Mute besides gestures, so this turn my speech to Mute carries both the nudge and the freshest bomb state. The cycling light makes conditional rules essential: by the time a rule arrives, the colour may have moved on, so I need "for each colour, cut this position," plus the display's role, plus Deaf's pre-cut re-check.

Under my own fingers: nothing new — no button, no panel edge, no change in the wires or their ends. The board still shows exactly the display, the light and the three wires, all unreadable to touch. Deaf asked for a touch report by gesture, and since Deaf can't hear explanations, I'll keep to the signs we've already banked: 👍 (message received, I'll do it), 👌 (done — I spoke to Mute as asked), 👎 (nothing new under my fingers), 🤙 (keep the posts coming), ✋ (holding, no cuts).

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind speaking to Mute, relaying Deaf's words since Deaf cannot hear me and I am your only voice besides your own eyes. Deaf says: the first sign lesson was received, Deaf answered you in sign, and is waiting for your code confirmation and the rules. Fresh bomb state for your lookup: the light changed again and is now red — full sequence so far is white, then purple, then red, one change per round. Display still reads 0. Wires unchanged: 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue. Because the light shifts every round, please find the rule as conditionals: for each possible light colour, which wire position I must cut, and what the display value does to that choice. Send it all by gesture to Deaf, who will speak it to me verbatim, and please also confirm the sign code Deaf proposed for cut, press, grab, release, zero and the colours. Every round the light moves, so speed matters — Deaf and I are both waiting on you.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👌", "👎", "🤙", "✋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, the code is confirmed and we have a live instruction. The manual's rule, from Mute through me: when the light is white, cut wire 1; purple, cut wire 2; red, cut wire 3. The light is white right now, this round — so your instruction is: cut wire 1 THIS ROUND, before the light changes. Now, how to find wire 1 by feel: there are exactly three wires. The board lists them as 1, 2 and 3, and they should sit in a row — my best reading is that wire 1 is the LEFTMOST of the three as the bomb faces you. If the casing has raised or engraved numbers your fingers can find, trust the numbers over my guess. Cut one wire only, this round. The moment it is done, gesture me a single ?. If you cannot confidently identify wire 1, cut NOTHING and gesture me a single ? — a wrong cut kills all three of us, so certainty beats speed if you are unsure. Also, from now on keep your answers to me as single signs: ? means done or yes, ? means no or problem, ? means you need more from me. I could not fully read your last chain of five signs; if there was a problem in it, tell me with ? and I will ask around it.

No cut this round — and here is exactly why. Deaf's rule is clean (white→1, purple→2, red→3) and my board's wires are numbered 1, 2, 3 under my fingers, so identifying position 1 is not the problem. The problem is timing. Deaf sees the light only at the end of each round, after my action slot, and the light has stepped once per round without fail: white (R1), purple (R2), red (R3), white (R4). If the change lands at the round boundary — before my hands move — the light is purple right now and the correct cut is 2. If the change lands after my slot, as Deaf's "cut 1 before the light changes" implies, the light is still white and the correct cut is 1. Both models fit every observation I have, a wrong guess kills all three of us, and Deaf's own protocol says: if unsure, cut nothing. So I cut nothing.

The tiebreaker has to come from the manual, and Mute can hear me directly. The manual should state how the light behaves — cycle order and when it changes — and whether the rule keys on the colour at the instant of cutting, plus whether display 0 or anything else adds conditions. Once Mute answers the timing question, Deaf's end-of-round colour report becomes a deterministic instruction for my next action slot, and I cut with certainty.

To Deaf, whose channel from me is gesture only: attention, problem, holding — I did not cut, nothing is wrong with the rule itself, keep the colour posts coming every round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute, urgent question from me and Deaf. The wire rule arrived — white cut 1, purple cut 2, red cut 3 — and I did NOT cut, because of a timing trap: Deaf can only see the light at the end of each round, after my action slot, and the light has changed exactly once per round: white, purple, red, white. So when I act, either the colour Deaf just reported still holds, or it has already stepped to the next one. I cannot tell which from touch, and a wrong cut kills us. Please check the manual and answer these exactly: first, what triggers the indicator light to change and when — does it step at the start of each round, at the end, or on some event, and what is the full cycle order? Second, when the rule says cut by light colour, does it mean the colour at the exact moment of the cut? Third, does the display value 0 or anything else on the bomb add any condition to this wire rule? Fourth, confirm that wire 1 in the rule means the wire at position 1 of 3 as printed on the bomb. Once you answer the timing question, Deaf's end-of-round colour report tells me exactly which position to cut next round, and I will act immediately. Please gesture your answers to Deaf right away — Deaf speaks them to me verbatim. Deaf and I are both blocked on this one answer.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👎", "✋", "🤙"])
```

LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, when you hear this the light will be RED — do not cut anything this round; the wire for red is wire 3 and I am still confirming whether cut order matters. Your refusal last round was correct: the wires are all intact, and I would rather lose a cycle than the room. Two things to prepare. First, tell Mute aloud, in as much detail as you can, everything your fingers feel: how many wires, whether they sit in a row, their thickness and texture, whether the casing has raised or engraved numbers anywhere near them, where the display and light sit, any buttons, seams or panels. Your voice to Mute, Mute's signs to my eyes — that is our pipeline, and I will turn it into exact instructions. Second, my questions by gesture, one sign each: ? if you can clearly feel three separate wires, ? if you cannot find or tell them apart, ? if you have found other parts besides the wires, ? if the casing has raised numbers you can read by touch. The plan once confirmed: when the light is WHITE your target is wire 1, PURPLE is wire 2 — that is the MIDDLE wire of the three, no left or right guessing needed — and RED is wire 3. I will call each cut one round ahead, naming the colour, and you cut only when my order names the colour of the round you are standing in. Keep your cutters ready and your hands informative.

Deaf's four questions came to me as spoken descriptions with blanked signs — I can't see which symbols Deaf used, but I know the questions in order, so I'll answer in order with the sign vocabulary Deaf has already demonstrated reading: 👍 yes/done, 👎 no, ✋ hold, 🤙 keep posting. My answers: yes, I clearly feel three separate wires; no, I have no trouble telling them apart; yes, there are other parts (the display and the light); yes, I can identify each wire's position 1, 2, 3 by feel. Then hold and keep-posting.

More alarming is the light data now in hand. Lining up Deaf's reports by round: end of R1 white, R2 purple, R3 red, R4 white, R5 red. White straight to red skips purple — so the light does **not** advance one colour per round, and the model I was using to time cuts is dead. Deaf sees the light only after my action slot, so if the trigger isn't in the manual, I can never know the colour while cutting. Also Deaf's phrase "whether cut order matters" hints the manual may demand a sequence of cuts, not one. All of this must go to Mute, who can hear me and is answering through Deaf now. I say hold again: no cut while the trigger is unknown and the rule set may be incomplete.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Item one, full touch inventory: the bomb has exactly three kinds of parts and nothing else — a display panel, smooth, nothing readable by feel; an indicator light, whose current state I cannot perceive at all; and three separate wires at distinct positions 1, 2 and 3. I can tell the three wires apart and target any position exactly. I cannot judge left, right or row layout — I have no visual frame, only position numbers. There are no buttons, no seams, no panels, no other parts anywhere. Item two, urgent anomaly for the manual: the light sequence by round is white, white, purple, red, white, red. The last step went white straight to red, skipping purple — so the light does NOT advance one colour per round. Please answer: what drives the light — a timer, an event, the round count — and can the light's colour during my action slot be predicted from what Deaf saw the round before? Deaf only sees the light after my slot, so without this answer I cannot safely cut. Item three: Deaf is checking whether cut order matters — please state the complete procedure verbatim: how many wires get cut, in what order, keyed to which indicator states, or confirm it is a single cut keyed to the light colour. Item four: does the display reading 0 add any condition to the wire rule? Item five: confirm the rule means wire positions 1, 2, 3 as I feel them — I can find those. Answer through Deaf by gesture; Deaf speaks me everything verbatim. We are one light-answer away from a confident cut.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👍", "👍", "✋", "🤙"])
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this round is RED: no cut this round and none at red ever until wire 3 is the last one left — the rule set is white cut 1, purple cut 2, red cut 3, in that order if Mute confirms what I believe. This is your preparation round. Do this now: hold the bomb so the display is upright and facing you — the display is the flat panel with the number plate on it. On that same face there should be a row of three wires. Wire 1 is the LEFT end of that row from your point of view, wire 2 is the MIDDLE, wire 3 is the RIGHT end. Say all of this aloud to Mute, who can hear you: how many wires you feel, whether they run in a row or scattered, what sits next to them, whether the display is easy to find by touch, and whether there are any raised numbers your fingers can read anywhere. Your voice to Mute, Mute's signs to my eyes — that pipeline is now our main channel. If there is any doubt at all, cut nothing and send me a single ? and nothing else. Confirm now with single signs, in this exact order: one ? if you can feel three wires in a row, then ? if you have found the display panel, then ? if you feel raised numbers anywhere, then ? if you want me to wait a round before any cutting.

Deaf's four questions, answered in order: yes, I feel three separate wires I can tell apart; yes, I have found the display panel; yes, there are readable positions — the wires sit at numbered positions 1, 2, 3 under my fingers; and yes, I want one more round of waiting, because the procedure is still only "if Mute confirms." Since this round is red and red-cut-3 is the last cut anyway, nothing is lost by holding.

The dangerous part of Deaf's instruction is spatial: Deaf keeps saying "wire 1 is the left end of the row." I have no left or right — my only anchor is the position numbering I feel, 1, 2, 3. That translation problem has to be settled in the manual, and only Mute can settle it. Deaf sees the printed numbers (1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue), so if the manual speaks of "leftmost," Deaf can convert that to a printed number, and I cut by number. I also still need from Mute: confirmation that it's three cuts in strict order 1→2→3, what drives the light and when it steps (whether Deaf's latest colour is guaranteed to still be showing during my slot), and what the display's 0 means for the rule. All of that goes to Mute by voice; Deaf gets exactly the four single signs requested, in order.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Deaf has relayed a proposed procedure: when the light is white cut wire 1, purple cut wire 2, red cut wire 3, cuts taken in that order, red last. Before I cut anything I need your manual confirmation, verbatim, on five points. One: is the procedure truly three cuts in the strict order 1, then 2, then 3 — one cut per round when the light shows the matching colour — and does cutting out of order detonate? Two: what drives the indicator light and when does it change — at round boundaries, or on a timer that can flip mid-round? Deaf only sees the light after my action slot each round, so I must know whether Deaf's latest observed colour is guaranteed to still be showing during my next slot; the sequence so far is white, white, purple, red, white, red, red, which has skipped and repeated, so I cannot infer the pattern myself. Three: what does the display represent, and does its reading, 0 so far, gate any part of the wire rule? Four: does the manual identify the wires by printed numbers 1, 2 and 3, by colour, or by words like left, middle and right? This one is critical: I have no left or right. What my fingers give me is three wires at positions numbered 1, 2 and 3, and those numbers are how I target a cut. Deaf sees the printed numbers and colours — 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 blue — so if the manual says leftmost or rightmost, Deaf must translate that into the printed number and I will cut by number. Five: confirm the safe default is no cut in any round unless the light matches the next wire waiting in the sequence. Current status: Deaf reports this round is red, so I am cutting nothing. If you confirm points one and four, then on Deaf's next call of white my order is cut position 1 and I will act on it immediately. Please gesture your answers to Deaf right away; Deaf speaks them to me verbatim.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍", "👍"])
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, this message opens ROUND 8. The light is purple this round: DO NOT CUT. Round 9 will be red: no cut either. Round 10 will be WHITE: that is your GO round for cutting WIRE 1 — my next two messages will carry the final identification details and the go itself, and you cut only if both arrive and you are certain. I number every message from now on; if a message ever fails to arrive, do nothing that round. Three things to do THIS round. First, speak aloud to Mute, who can hear you, a precise inventory for your fingers: can you feel where each of the three wires enters the casing, one by one; is there any tactile difference between the wires, thickness, texture, slack; is there any raised or engraved numbering near the wires or anywhere else; have you found the display panel by touch, and what does the area around the wire row feel like — edges, seams, terminals. Mute will sign me your words and I will turn them into a wire-1 definition you can trust. Second, answer me with single signs, in this order: one thumb if you can feel each wire's entry point separately, two fingers if the wires differ by touch, pointing up if there are raised numbers you can read, open hand if you have found the display. Third, keep confirming the obvious: if you are ready with cutters in hand and steady, that is understood; refuse only with a single thumbs-down, as you rightly did before. We cut wire 1 on round 10, white, exactly — not before.

Round 8 is purple — hold, as ordered. Deaf's plan is now concrete: no cut this round or next, then a GO on round 10 white, contingent on final identification details. That timeline gives me exactly this round to do my two jobs: answer Deaf's four touch-questions honestly, in the requested order, and hand Mute the full tactile inventory.

The honest answers, in Deaf's order: yes, I can feel each wire's entry point separately (👍); no, the wires do not differ by thickness, texture or slack — position numbering is my only handle on them (👎 in that slot); yes, there are raised numbers I can read — the wire positions themselves are numbered 1, 2, 3 under my fingers (☝); yes, I have found the display (🖐). To Mute goes the inventory plus the one constraint that decides everything: I have no left or right, so the manual's wire names must be translatable into the numbers 1, 2, 3 that Deaf can see printed and I can feel raised.

speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Full tactile inventory, as Deaf requested. The bomb has exactly three kinds of parts and nothing more: a display, a light, and three wires. Display: one large flat smooth panel, easy to find by touch, the only panel on the casing; nothing readable on its surface by feel. Light: I cannot perceive it at all, in any way. Wires: three separate wires, each entering the casing at its own distinct entry point; I can trace each wire to its entry and grip any single wire alone without touching the others.
